speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Threepence for the bench again, Master Shakespeare. Sunday was the first. This is the second. I am not offering a third with the dish in my hand.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Count the second. The dish can stay a dish.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Herring. The loaf is the penny one, short by a finger, as it was. And those hose on the chair are not from any London shop. I can see the stitch from the door.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: A mother's stitch. Did the carrier take anything, or only bring the hose?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: He took four lines. Wednesday, by Oxford, the bridge on Friday by dusk. He leaves today, and he is there before me. The hose stayed.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Four lines is a letter a house can use. The full page is still on your board. I saw it this morning, face down, and I left it face down.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Is that still the page I cannot read? I am not asking to be given it. I am asking if it is the same one.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The same one. It has no day in it. It did not go. You could not read it if you were required to, Alse, and you are not.

speaker: gillis_verbeke
text: I will take the herring and leave the letters to the people who write them. A Saturday table is a good place to be quiet.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: You were at a book again. Is there a plot I am owed, or is it still a shut page?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: No plot. A shape, and no one speaking in it. I am not bringing it down to the table.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Then I am not owed a verdict. I have had the one I have had. Keep the new one until it is a story.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: If nobody speaks, there is nothing for me to ask you to say again. I can live with the herring.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Live with the herring. Threepence is the meal. The road is next week, and the road is not this dish.

speaker: gillis_verbeke
text: Next week the loom will not know you are gone until the stair is quiet. I will notice the quiet. That is all I mean to say about a journey.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: The firing sixpence runs till Lady Day, which is Tuesday, and I am not collecting it over herring. What becomes of the chamber is a Tuesday question.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: I am not asking you to let it or to keep it. I will be a few days, not a quarter. The four lines have the days in them.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: Shall I move the hose off the chair, or are they meant to be seen?

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: They are meant to be worn when I am home. Until then the chair can hold them. Thank you, Alse.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Threepence when you pass the stair. Two meals this week, and a letter that went, and a letter that did not. I can count that without a sermon.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Two meals. One letter gone. One letter still. I am not starting a speech before I go out tonight.

speaker: alse_pinder
text: I will leave the hose on the chair, and the page on the board.

speaker: gillis_verbeke
text: Then the house can be quiet, which is how a loom likes a house. Good afternoon.

speaker: dorcas_ansell
text: Good afternoon. The board stays as it is unless you take the page off it yourself.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: The board stays. The second threepence is the meal, and the meal is done.
